title: Correctness: ioctl_key_generate -EBUSY path does not clear inbuf (asymmetry with key_import)
description:
Trigger: open() fd → write(key_bytes) → KEY_GENERATE (fd is already initialized → -EBUSY).

In ioctl_key_generate, the state->fd_type != FDTYPE_UNSET (-EBUSY) check jumps to 'out:' which only does mutex_unlock — inbuf_clear is NOT called on this path.

By contrast, ioctl_key_import on its -EBUSY path jumps to 'out_inbuf_clear' which does clear the inbuf.

The practical impact is currently zero: write() on a non-UNSET fd returns -ENODEV for KEY fds and routes through update() for OPERATION fds (no inbuf accumulation). So when KEY_GENERATE fires -EBUSY, inbuf is always empty in practice.

However the asymmetry is a latent correctness issue: if the fd type or write() routing ever changes, the inbuf would not be cleared on the -EBUSY path in KEY_GENERATE. The fix is to call inbuf_clear(state) on all KEY_GENERATE error paths inside the lock, matching the pattern used in KEY_IMPORT.
close_reason: Added inbuf_clear(state) on KEY_GENERATE -EBUSY path inside the lock, matching the pattern used by ioctl_key_import
